title: 1.4 Major Geological Processes
description: Endogenic and exogenic forces, folding, faulting, earthquakes, tsunamis and volcanism. Easy level.

questions.question: What are endogenic forces?
options: Forces that originate inside the Earth
Forces that originate in the atmosphere
questions.correctAnswer: Forces that originate inside the Earth

questions.question: What are exogenic forces?
options: An increase in desert conditions from overgrazing and cultivation
The North American Plate includes western North Atlantic seafloor
Orbital variations help initiate glacial and interglacial periods
Forces that originate outside the Earth, mainly in the atmosphere
questions.correctAnswer: Forces that originate outside the Earth, mainly in the atmosphere

questions.question: What is folding?
options: The lack of a plausible mechanism for continental movement
Adaptation that takes place before impacts become apparent
The bending of rock layers due to sideways earth movements
Tropical regions where many developing nations are located
questions.correctAnswer: The bending of rock layers due to sideways earth movements

questions.question: What is a fault?
options: A crack in the Earth crust
questions.correctAnswer: A crack in the Earth crust

questions.question: What is a rift valley?
options: Land between two faults that has sunk down
Land between two faults that has risen
It was the coldest century in a millennium
Human influence will continue to change it
questions.correctAnswer: Land between two faults that has sunk down

questions.question: What is a block mountain also called?
What is an earthquake?
options: Changes systems undergo in response to climate regardless of any policy or plan
Sudden ground shaking caused by rock masses changing position below the surface
They interact at boundaries to form features such as mountains and earthquakes
A change in the mean or variability of climate persisting for decades or longer
questions.correctAnswer: Sudden ground shaking caused by rock masses changing position below the surface
